newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia cargo craft fails to dock with Mir-Tass.
newsitem.headline: Russia cargo craft fails to dock with Mir-Tass.

text.p: A Progress-M-33 cargo rocket carrying supplies to the Russian space station Mir failed to complete a planned docking with the manned orbiting module on Tuesday, Itar-Tass news agency said.

It quoted a mission control spokesman saying experts were looking into the reasons for the failure. Mission control could not immediately be reached for comment. Russians Vasily Tsibliyev and Alexander Lazutkin and U.S. astronaut Jerry Linenger are on Mir at the moment.

Tass later said the Progress had de-docked on February 6 to make way for a Soyuz TM-25 carrying a replacement crew. That craft brought two Russians and a German cosmonaut back to Earth on Sunday, leaving room for the Progress to re-dock.
The problem, which Tass said was the second failed attempt, would be the second hitch in just over a week to trouble the 11-year-old Mir, which has already outlived its expected span.
On February 23, a fire broke out on board, forcing the crew, to don gas masks.

Once the jewel in the crown of the Soviet Union's military-dominated industry, Russia's space agency is suffering a severe cash crisis which last week prompted it to postpone the launch of its first contribution to a planned international space station, Alpha, which will replace Mir.
